assessment: This study provides important new insights into how learning affects behavior in the Drosophila model. Using a combination of connectomics, neurophysiology, and behavioral analysis, a small group of neurons in the Drosophila brain that integrates learned odor valences and promotes odor tracking by driving upwind orientation and movement is described. The study's conclusion is supported by convincing evidence and rigorous quantitative analysis. Insights from the neural circuit mechanism that translates learning-induced plasticity into appropriate behavioral actions will be of broad interest to neuroscientists.
